text: Tomb A2 at Jericho, on Hill A. A rock-cut tomb with a pit, benches and six kokhim, the only one of its kind. The entrance faces north. Primary burials lay in the kokhim, whose walls were faced with clay; collected bones of infants and children lay in the pit. In a later phase the kokhim were sealed with plaster and the tomb was a single chamber with benches and a shallow pit. Seven ossuaries were then placed on the plastered benches. An ossuary inscription gives the name Yehosef. The report dates the tomb's ossuary burials to the early first century CE until 68 CE, and its earliest phase possibly to the first century BCE.

Tomb D1 at Jericho, on Hill D. A rock-cut tomb with a pit, benches and three kokhim: two on the north (one small) and one in the west wall; the south side collapsed into Tomb D17. It was cut above two kokhim of Tomb D9 and is later than it. Four ossuaries and an inscribed bowl. Inscriptions on the bowl and on two ossuaries give the names Ishma'el son of Shim'on son of Palta from Jerusalem, Pelatya from Jerusalem, and Simon with his age. The report dates the tomb to the early first century CE until 68 CE.

Tomb D2 at Jericho, on Hill D, in Tomb Complex D. The entrance faces east and was sealed with a stopper-type blocking stone. A small courtyard was cut in front of the tomb. A pit, benches and seven kokhim, five large and two small ones added later. Wooden coffins with primary burials lay in the five large kokhim and on a bench; kokhim were sealed with stones and plaster, two with flat slabs. Bones of two to six individuals were collected in one small kokh. The report dates the tomb to the first century BCE, perhaps continuing into the early first century CE.

Tomb D3 at Jericho, on Hill D, above Tomb Complex D and later than it. The entrance faces east and was blocked by a large stopper-type blocking stone; the tomb had been entered earlier through a hole above it. A small courtyard was cut in front of the tomb. A large shallow pit, benches and six kokhim. Collected bones (secondary burials) lay in all the kokhim, with no burial containers. The report dates the tomb to the early first century CE until 68 CE.

Tomb D9 at Jericho, on Hill D. A single chamber and seven kokhim, without a pit or benches, high enough to stand in. Kokhim were sealed with a heavy rectangular stone or with mudbricks. Wooden coffins with primary burials lay in the kokhim and on the chamber floor. The report dates the tomb to the first century BCE, perhaps continuing into the early first century CE.

Tomb D10 at Jericho, on Hill D, in Tomb Complex D, on the upper level. The entrance faces east. The ceiling is missing; the tomb was filled with soil, debris and a few scattered bones. The report dates the tomb to the first century BCE, perhaps continuing into the early first century CE.

Tomb D11 at Jericho, on Hill D, in Tomb Complex D. A single-kokh tomb above the platform, reached by steps. The entrance faces east and was still sealed with a sealing stone, soil and plaster. Fragments of a wooden coffin with one primary burial. The report dates the tomb to the first century BCE, perhaps continuing into the early first century CE.

Tomb D12 at Jericho, on Hill D, in Tomb Complex D. The entrance faces east and was still sealed by a large flat blocking slab with plaster and stones; incised lines above the arched entrance may imitate a masonry arch. A small courtyard was cut in front of the tomb. A pit, benches and three kokhim, two in the north wall and one in the west wall. Seven wooden coffins with primary burials lay on the benches, in the pit and in the kokhim; kokhim were sealed with plastered blocking stones and a large plastered slab. The report dates the tomb to the first century BCE, perhaps continuing into the early first century CE.

Tomb D14 at Jericho, on Hill D, in Tomb Complex D. A single-kokh tomb, the last cut on the platform, sealed with small stones, soil and plaster. Tomb D16 at Jericho, on Hill D, in Tomb Complex D. A single-kokh tomb located north of Tomb D11. The entrance is in the north; the lower part of its seal survived. Tomb D17 at Jericho, on Hill D. The entrance is approached from the east through a small rock-cut courtyard or passage with a small bench; it was sealed with a blocking stone in situ, in a recessed door frame. Six kokhim, a small kokh opening from one of them, and a pit. Ossuary fragments and bones in the debris probably came from Tomb D13 above; no burials were found in the kokhim. The report dates the tomb to the early first century CE until 68 CE.

Tomb D18 at Jericho, on Hill D, on a lower level south of Tomb Complex D. A stopper-type blocking stone lay near the entrance; the ceiling had collapsed. A small courtyard was cut in front of the tomb. Six kokhim blocked with stones, benches and a pit. Wooden coffins with primary burials lay on the benches and in the kokhim; coins of Yehohanan Hyrcanus I and Herod Archelaus were found. Not completely excavated. The report dates the tomb to the first century BCE, perhaps continuing into the early first century CE.
Tomb D21 at Jericho, on Hill D. A single-kokh tomb bordering Tomb D17, full of collected bones (secondary burials). The report dates the tomb to the early first century CE until 68 CE.

Six kokhim and no pit, the ceiling being high enough to stand; kokhim were sealed with stones and bricks. Primary burials lay on the floor, and in wooden coffins in the kokhim. The report dates the tomb to the first century BCE, perhaps continuing into the early first century CE.

Tomb H at Jericho, on Hill H: the Goliath family tomb. A large courtyard with benches, a mourning enclosure of the Herodian period, lies in front of the tomb, with a miqveh fed by a small channel from the Na'aran water channel. A corridor leads to the entrance, which was blocked by two large sealing stones; it has a masonry lintel and doorjambs, the only masonry entrance found at Jericho. The tomb has two connecting chambers. Chamber A has a standing pit, benches, eight kokhim and a bone repository holding the bones of about 100 individuals. The entrance of Chamber A is in its east wall, next to the bone repository. Chamber B, lower, has six kokhim and no pit. The plastered walls of Chamber A are painted with vine branches, birds and probably a pergola. Twenty-two ossuaries. Ossuary inscriptions in Greek and Jewish script give the names Yeho'ezer son of Ele'azar, Goliath, Shelamsiyon, Ishma'el, Simon, Menahem, Natan'el, Maria, Mariame, Salome, Judah and Aqaby'a. One ossuary inscription names Theodotos, freedman of Queen Agrippina. A Greek abecedary in charcoal is inscribed inside an ossuary lid. The report dates the tomb's ossuary burials to the early first century CE until 68 CE, the finds from the tomb and its courtyard to the second half of the first century CE, and a reopening of the tomb to the late first or early second century CE.

text: Stone nefesh fragment found on the surface of Hill D at Jericho, out of its original context (Cat. No. 422). A three-faceted fragment: a fluted column topped by a fluted ring and a cone decorated with lozenges; two holes may have held a metal plaque. The report reads it as a nefesh, a column-pyramid that served as the marker on a tomb.
